name: Tony Hawk
bio: Landed the first-ever 900 at the 1999 X Games. Built a billion-dollar brand and brought skateboarding to the mainstream through video games, media, and philanthropy. Widely considered the most famous skateboarder of all time.

name: Rodney Mullen
bio: Invented the flat-ground ollie, kickflip, heelflip, 360 flip, and dozens of foundational street tricks. Nearly every modern street trick traces back to Mullen's innovations. A quiet genius who transformed skateboarding's vocabulary.

name: Jay Adams
bio: The most naturally talented of the Z-Boys who revolutionized skateboarding in the 1970s. His aggressive, improvisational surf-style in empty pools defined the raw soul of skateboarding.

name: Tony Alva
bio: Z-Boys legend and the first skater to do a frontside air above a pool's coping. Founded Alva Skateboards, one of the first skater-owned brands. Embodied punk-rock rebellion in skating.

name: Stacy Peralta
bio: Z-Boys member turned visionary team manager. Assembled the Bones Brigade — the greatest skate team ever — and directed iconic skate videos. Later became an acclaimed filmmaker with 'Dogtown and Z-Boys'.

name: Nyjah Huston
bio: The most dominant competitive street skater in history. Known for fearless big-rail skating and machine-like consistency. Highest-earning contest skater of all time.

name: Mark Gonzales
bio: Pioneer of modern street skating who treated the urban landscape as art. His creative, boundary-pushing approach in 'Video Days' redefined what skateboarding could be. Also a celebrated visual artist and poet.

name: Alan Gelfand
bio: Invented the ollie — popping the board into the air without using your hands — the single most important trick in skateboarding history. Every modern trick builds on the ollie.

name: Steve Caballero
bio: Bones Brigade legend who invented the Caballerial (fakie 360 ollie). One of the most versatile skaters ever, excelling at vert, street, and pool. Still skating at the highest level decades later.

name: Lance Mountain
bio: Bones Brigade member known for his joyful, creative approach. Famous for painting over his own board sponsors for fun. Embodied the idea that skating should always be about fun first.

name: Leticia Bufoni
bio: Most decorated female street skater and the most-followed female skateboarder on social media. Multiple X Games gold medalist who inspired a generation of women to pick up a board.

name: Yuto Horigome
bio: Won the first-ever Olympic gold medal in skateboarding at the 2020 Tokyo Games. Known for impossibly precise ledge tricks and a calm, methodical competition style. Represents Japan's emergence as a street skating powerhouse.

name: Sky Brown
bio: Won Olympic bronze at age 13, becoming one of the youngest Olympic medalists in history. A global youth icon who also surfs competitively. Represents the new generation of multi-sport action athletes.

name: Bob Burnquist
bio: Brazilian vert legend known for his backyard mega ramp and fearless innovation. Pioneer of switch vert skating. Holds the record for most X Games medals of any skateboarder.

name: Paul Rodriguez Jr.
bio: Son of comedian Paul Rodriguez, P-Rod became one of the most marketable skaters ever. His groundbreaking sponsorship deals ushered in the era of skaters as mainstream athletes with corporate endorsements.

name: Rob Dyrdek
bio: Transitioned from pro skater to media mogul and entrepreneur. Created Street League Skateboarding (SLS), professionalizing competitive street skating with standardized judging and major prize money.

name: Danny Way
bio: Mega ramp innovator who jumped the Great Wall of China on a skateboard. Holds numerous big air records and helped design the DC Mega Ramp. Known for skating through catastrophic injuries.
accolades: Jumped the Great Wall of China

name: Momiji Nishiya
bio: Won Olympic gold in women's street at age 13, becoming one of the youngest Olympic gold medalists in any sport. Part of Japan's remarkable sweep in street skateboarding at the Tokyo Games.
